<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Examining the club matrix frontend type to understand how leagues are derived.

Checking existing navigationQuery tests and design system chip patterns. The `myClub` parameter will be global and persist in the URI until deselected. Minimal backend changes are needed for tournament filtering.

The UI will place a MyClub selector near the search bar with a visual indicator banner. When active, a creative ribbon or chip will appear in the main content area alongside a sidebar pin.

Client-side filtering will use the club matrix to extract unique season and league pairs. This restricts available seasons and leagues in LeagueStats. Team lists will be limited to the club's own teams. Standings and results will show only events where at least one club member participated.

Clarifying whether result tables themselves need filtering. The requirement likely means showing only the club's teams' perspective within each league, rather than merely restricting the candidate list. Season filtering may also apply to the results view.

Leagues and tournaments will both be filtered to events where the club had a participant. The season dropdown will list only seasons where the club had a team. The league dropdown will list only leagues where the club participated. The team dropdown will list only teams belonging to that club.

Invalid selections will be cleared when the myClub filter activates. For tournament filtering, a thin service method extending existing endpoints is preferable to a new route. This keeps changes within the service layer rather than data access.

Leagues will be fully client-side from the club matrix. Tournament filtering will use an optional `club` query parameter on existing endpoints, matching the Club column NFC. Still deciding whether to hide other teams in standings tables or simply restrict the candidate list.

Interpreting "filtered results" as restricting event lists and the team filter, not hiding other teams from standings. Full standings remain visible while the team dropdown narrows to club teams. Considering whether league overview cards and latest events should also be club-relevant. Re-examining LeagueStats and season overview to confirm.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have a clear plan and am ready to implement the myClub feature.

The `myClub` query parameter will persist globally without sanitization. A `useMyClub` hook will manage its state. The sidebar will host a club search with a creative active indicator. League filtering will derive participation from the club matrix and apply client-side. Tournament filtering will use a backend `club` parameter.

The `myClub` parameter avoids clashing with the existing `/club` route. For tournament filtering, club labels will be normalized with NFC normalization and matched against the selected club or history club. Player records may use slightly different labels, so the matching logic needs to handle minor variations.

Exact NFC matching on the tournament Club column is the pragmatic first cut for MVP. Affiliation-based filtering would be more accurate but requires heavier data access. Substring matching was rejected.

The active club selection will automatically clear the league filter when the current league is outside the club’s participation pool. The latest season will be resolved automatically for the selected club. The visual indicator will be a “home pin” ribbon with a primary left accent bar, a home icon, and the club name in semibold monospace.

The banner will include an X button to deselect the club. A subtle animated accent stripe will mark the active state. The club search will sit in the sidebar under a "Mein Club" label. The active club will render as a sticky banner at the top of the main content area. Three files will be created: a myClub utility module, a useMyClub hook, and a MyClubBanner component.

A `MyClubControl` component will handle the sidebar search and selection. `Sidebar`, `App.tsx`, and `navigationQuery` need updates to preserve `myClub`. `LeagueStats`, `SeasonLeagueStandings`, `TournamentStats`, and `useTournament` will receive club filters. Backend tournament routes and services will support the new parameter. Client-side filtering suffices for available leagues. There is an open question about whether selecting a club on the `/club` page should also set `myClub`.

The myClub fuzzy search will remain independent from the page-level club filter. Selecting a club there will not automatically set myClub. When myClub activates, the league, week, team, and round filters will be cleared if they fall outside the club’s participation pool. The season will reset to the latest among the club’s seasons. The teams query will be filtered to teams belonging to the selected club.

I need to align the club matrix league names with the available leagues API. The matrix uses full names like "Bayernliga", while the API returns short and long variants. I will verify the exact mapping before filtering.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

**Mein Club** is wired as a global lens via `?myClub=…`.

### How it works
- **Sidebar** — fuzzy club search under “Mein Club”; selection writes `myClub` into the URL
- **Banner** — teal ticket-stub ribbon across every page (`Mein Club` + club name + clear)
- **Persistence** — `myClub` is **not** stripped by the route sanitizer (unlike page-local `club=`); only clearing it removes it
- **Liga** — seasons / leagues / teams come from the club matrix; season overview shows only those leagues
- **Turnier** — `club=` on seasons / tournaments / podiums APIs (match on Club / History Club)

### Try it
`/liga?myClub=Donaubowler%20Regensburg` — league dropdown should shrink to that club’s leagues; navigate away and `myClub` stays until you clear it.

### Later (myPlayer)
Same pattern: a `myPlayer` query key, parallel control/banner, and player-scoped event filters.

Club-filtered Spieler all-time caches are now part of player cache warming.

**What was added**
- Phase `myclub-spieler` / `myclub-spieler-batch` in `scripts/warm_player_cache.py` — for each canonical club warms search, seasons, lifetime `season=all`, highest games, and club-300 (same stack as `/spieler?myClub=…`).
- `warm_cache_shard.py --warm-players` shards all **129** league clubs (11 batches via `--clubs-per-shard`, default 12) using the league catalog club list so keys match Mein Club names.

**How to run**
```bash
# one club
uv run python scripts/warm_player_cache.py --database db_player_merged_hybrid --phase myclub-spieler --club "Donaubowler Regensburg"

# all clubs (via shard orchestrator)
uv run python scripts/warm_cache_shard.py --database db_real_merged --warm-players --max-parallel 8
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Rewriting the club filter function to match games by club instead of players' lifetime records. The function will be renamed to `_filter_df_to_club_games`. Search results will then use distinct players from those filtered games.

Club names will be resolved through LeagueService for consistency with NFC matching. The old `_club_roster_ids_and_names` helper can be removed entirely. A new `_resolve_club_label` method will normalize the club identifier.

The resolver method now queries available clubs via `LeagueService` and falls back to the raw input if no match exists. The new `_filter_df_to_club_games` helper validates inputs and imports internal club normalization utilities.

The implementation resolves the club label and normalizes it with `_normalize_club_label`. It then filters the DataFrame using `_club_series` to keep only rows where the normalized club matches. The developer is considering whether to include History Club entries since the user wants games specifically for that club.

History Club entries are excluded from the filter because the user wants only league games. Tournament rows may still appear if they match the club label. The search_players method will apply the club filter to the full player dataframe.

Rather than building a separate catalog from the filtered games, the existing player catalog will be filtered directly. Unique player IDs and names will be extracted from the club-games subset, preserving canonical names without extra registry logic.

Cache versions for player search, season availability, lifetime stats, highest individual games, and club 300 records will be bumped. A small unit test with real data may be added. Docstrings and frontend copy mentioning "alumni" will be updated to reflect the new club-based filtering.</details></think>
